claims.text: (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 exhibits a large caloric response under applied magnetic fields.
(MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 exhibits a large caloric response under applied pressure fields.
(MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 has poor mechanical integrity, brittleness, and susceptibility to cracking.
Modified solidification or thermomechanical processing can induce an in-situ second phase in the alloy.
The induced second phase will be ductile, finely dispersed, and continuous along grain boundaries.
The proposed processing will produce a dual-phase microstructure while retaining the primary caloric phase.
A ductile grain-boundary network will absorb and blunt stress concentrations.
The ductile grain-boundary network will arrest crack propagation during mechanical loading.
The second phase will not interfere with the phase transition responsible for the caloric effect.
The dual-phase modification will increase compressive strength relative to the conventionally processed alloy.
The modified alloy may approach or surpass a compressive-strength range of 152–218 MPa.
Epoxy-containing comparison systems previously exhibited compressive strengths in the 152–218 MPa range.
The modification will improve fracture resistance relative to the unchanged alloy.
The modified alloy will maintain a caloric-response magnitude comparable to that of the unchanged alloy.
The expected improvements will persist under magnetic and pressure fields near the caloric transition temperature and under typical mechanical loading.
Operation outside the calibrated processing or operating window may produce different phases.
Introducing the second phase may cause minor changes in transition temperature or caloric-effect magnitude.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and mechanism state that the intervention will not degrade or interfere with the caloric response, whereas the uncertainty and falsification rule allow a minor caloric-performance compromise.
